topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The forest hums, a low whisper under the broad sweep of the sky. I approach the clearing; the scent of fresh cut wood bites the air, sharp and raw. The shape that once towered, a friend in the dance of seasons, is gone. Only the stump remains, a broad disk speaking of the past. The edges of the clearing seem to close in, the silence pressing close. I circle the stump, the patterns of roots and earth telling a story now cut short. The air tastes of change, the kind that leaves an echo in the heart of the woods, a lingering absence where once there was more. I pause, ears and nose working, every sense alert, before moving on, the world transformed and shrinking around me.
